# TinyStories
**Type:** Measurement  
**Referenced in:** 11 papers  
**Also known as:** Tiny Stories  

## State of the Field

**What it is.** Across the surveyed work, TinyStories is most commonly described as a synthetic dataset of short or children's stories, often generated by GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. Definitions repeatedly frame it as small enough for tractable training, especially for small or medium-scale models, while still presenting text-generation challenges such as coherence and narrative structure. Some authors describe it more generally as short, simple stories generated by a large language model, and one paper specifies that it uses around 1500 English words a child might use.

**What it is claimed to measure.** Papers link TinyStories to two behavioral indicators, Text generation and Creative writing, and no constructs are linked to it. The prevailing usage is to measure Text generation, with papers training or evaluating models on language generation, story continuation, and prefix-suffix generation from unseen stories. A smaller line of work reports it as measuring Creative writing through story-continuation experiments and broader evaluation suites.

**Space of uses.** Papers commonly use TinyStories as a practical training and evaluation corpus, and one study notes that its small size makes model training and aggregating N-gram statistics computationally efficient. It is sometimes paired with other datasets, for example combined with Children Stories for training or used alongside ROCStories for character choices, and it also appears in experiment suites with CNN/Daily Mail and GSM8K. One evaluation setup uses prefix-suffix snippets from an evaluation set of 100 unseen stories.
